text:
maria: quick sync — proposing we split batch-shaping responsibility between the router and the scheduler. router stays cheap: attach a small `shape_hint` to each request (latency_sensitive | throughput_bulk | no_hint). scheduler uses hints + a short-term traffic sketch to pick window length and max_batch_size. prevents heavy per-request CPU in router and keeps the scheduling policy centralized but informed.

kevin: curious — how do we prevent clients from gaming `latency_sensitive`? also worried about hint propagation cost if we add more metadata.

maria: good call. plan is router only accepts hints from authenticated clients or our internal gateways. for external, we do a lite classifier in the router that tags `no_hint` -> `probable_latency` only if request size/past_timing matches. classifier is O(1) heuristic, no model.

sasha: we need observability before we roll this. want counters: hints_received_by_type, hint_vs_actual_latency, misclassified_rate. add a histogram for scheduler window_ms chosen vs p99.

alex: experiment idea: A/B two schedulers — one uses hints+sketch predictor, other uses baseline fixed-window. 24h, same load shape. metrics: p50/p90/p99 tokens/sec, token-cost, batch_utilization, and tail latency.

maria: agreed. quick draft config snippet for router/scheduler exchange:
```
router:
  add_header: X-Shape-Hint: "{{shape_hint}}"
  hint_policy: authenticated_only

scheduler:
  predictors:
    - name: shortterm_histogram
      lookback_ms: 5000
  defaults:
    max_batch_tokens: 1024
    window_ms: 10
```

kevin: nit: use ms windows that are powers of two multiples? easier to bucket in telemetry. also add a fallback `max_wait_ms` to avoid starvation when stream is sparse.

sasha: question about fairness — if throughput_bulk requests get big windows, could latency_sensitive requests on same GPU starve? we need admission caps by hint label or per-tenant budgeting.

maria: yes — scheduler will maintain per-hint soft quotas. enforcement is lightweight: admission credits per hint with periodic refill. we avoid hard evictions but will prefer smaller windows for latency-sensitive when headroom tight.

alex: ran quick lab run on bench with mixed mix (30% latency_sensitive, 70% throughput). early numbers: baseline fixed-window p99 320ms, hinted scheduler p99 210ms, batch_utilization up 12%, token-cost down ~6%. these are noisy but promising.

kevin: nice. do we have a regression signal for quality when we change batch sizes (some models are sensitive to prefix batching)? need to ensure reroutes to a held-back variant on anomalies.

sasha: add eval hooks: per-slice sampling of outputs for semantic drift and a rollback trigger if soft thresholds hit. tie that into Rollouts in the console.

maria: action items: (1) alex & kevin to run 48h A/B and produce a short dashboard (2) sasha to spec telemetry + rollback hooks (3) devex to add router header docs and authenticated hint policy. I'll draft a follow-up RFC with config examples and experiment results.

runtime-bot: deploy accepted: routers/hint-proxy v3.0 -> canary started :rocket:

kevin: :thumbsup: lemme know when canary reached 5% so I can start the A/B profiling.

maria: will post canary % and sample dashboard links once available. thanks everyone :eyes:
